question: A 34-year-old patient with moderate-to-severe Crohn's disease has failed azathioprine and is being considered for infliximab. Before initiating infliximab, which of the following pre-treatment screens is MANDATORY and why?

answers.text: Tuberculin skin test (TST) or IGRA, because infliximab's TNF-α blockade impairs granuloma maintenance and can reactivate latent TB with potentially fatal outcome

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. TNF-α is essential for granuloma formation that walls off latent Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Infliximab and other anti-TNF biologics disrupt this defence, reactivating latent TB — sometimes as disseminated or extrapulmonary TB. Latent TB must be identified and treated (usually with isoniazid for 6–9 months) before starting anti-TNF therapy.

answers.text: Serum potassium, because infliximab causes hyperkalaemia by inhibiting renal TNF receptors involved in potassium excretion

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Infliximab is not associated with hyperkalaemia via renal mechanisms. Electrolyte disturbances are not a primary pre-screening concern for anti-TNF initiation.

answers.text: Liver biopsy, because infliximab is hepatotoxic and liver histology must confirm adequate hepatic reserve before dosing

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While LFTs are checked and hepatitis B serology is screened before infliximab, a liver biopsy is not required. TB screening (TST/IGRA) is the most critical mandatory pre-treatment investigation.

answers.text: Colonoscopy to grade disease activity, because infliximab is only licensed for endoscopically confirmed severe disease

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. While endoscopic confirmation of Crohn's is part of diagnosis, it is not a regulatory requirement immediately before each biologic initiation. The mandatory safety screen before anti-TNF therapy is TB testing — failing to do so risks life-threatening TB reactivation.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review the biologics section and the clinical pearl on TB screening. TNF-α blockade disables granuloma integrity — every anti-TNF biologic carries this mandatory pre-treatment screen, and in India's high-TB-burden context it is non-negotiable.

Critical safety point. In India, where TB prevalence is high, the TB screen before anti-TNF biologics is even more important. Prescribing infliximab without excluding latent TB can convert a controlled infection into a rapidly progressive, often extrapulmonary disease.
